backtest_protocol.execution_model: Signal uses only PIT SEC filing event rows with report_date, filing_date, accepted_at, and usable_trade_date plus close-of-day OHLCV available on the signal date. Paper entry is next available open with existing entry slippage; exit is the close 10 trading days after the signal with target-side sell slippage and ROUND_TRIP_COST_PCT.
backtest_protocol.source: docs/backtesting.md canonical three-window core replay plus replay-only broad warehouse default-off paper overlay

gate3.note: No new core filter or entry rule was added. The pressure resilience candidate source is additive default-off paper, so core signals generated/survived are unchanged from baseline.

gate3_survival_note: Core survival is checked by BASE_GATE4. Target survival is a default-off overlay candidate sample; no live/core filter is added.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: candidate_pool: PIT SEC 10-Q/10-K filings with unusually fast filing lag (10-Q <= 30 days, 10-K <= 55 days from report_date to filing_date), when same-day OHLCV leadership confirms absorption, may identify higher-quality timely reporters whose next-open continuation adds replacement value beyond generic periodic-report momentum.

2_history_check.exp-20260601-027: Accepted Companyfacts filing timeliness support. This is the positive historical lead: test whether a directly PIT SEC event timeliness field can form a candidate pool rather than only support an existing fundamental-growth sleeve.
2_history_check.exp-20260611-012: Rejected generic periodic-report absorption leadership: 9 trades, aggregate EV -0.0545, PnL -$172.82, and failed accepted compression/distribution comparators. This run does not retry all periodic filings; it adds a fixed fast-filing timing gate.
2_history_check.exp-20260611-017: Rejected quantified counterparty commitment text. This run uses no SEC text, LLM, named-counterparty, or item-label scoring.
2_history_check.exp-20260611-025: Rejected SEC capital-market financing confirmation: only 2 target trades and comparator failure. This run avoids financing item-code semantics entirely.

gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: Gate 1-4 per docs/backtesting.md on late_strong, mid_weak, and old_thin. Aggregate EV/PnL must be positive, drawdown/survival cannot materially worsen, at least two windows should improve, target sample and concentration must pass, and accepted compression/distribution candidate-source comparators must be beaten. A positive replay result is not accepted for production until shared-helper parity exists.

interpretation: The SEC periodic filing timing source was rejected; it did not establish a distinct free SEC event/OHLCV candidate-pool edge under the standard three-window protocol.
negative_reflection: If rejected, the likely reason is that fast periodic filing lag is a quality/timeliness attribute already embedded in large liquid reporters or already priced by earnings release timing. It may support an existing fundamental sleeve but not stand alone after next-open execution, costs, cooldown, and accepted source comparators. Do not answer by sweeping lag thresholds, adding amendments, weakening price-confirmation guards, or changing top-N/hold/notional on frozen windows.
next_evidence_needed: A retry needs materially new PIT timing evidence, such as ticker-specific historical filing cadence relative to its own prior deadlines, auditor-change context, or forward daily replacement value from a shared default-off adapter. Pure 10-Q/10-K lag threshold retunes stay frozen.

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not retry by sweeping 10-Q/10-K lag cutoffs, including amendments, changing top-N/hold/notional/cooldown, or weakening same-day leadership gates on these frozen windows.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A retry needs materially new PIT timing evidence, such as ticker-specific historical filing cadence relative to its own prior deadlines, auditor-change context, or forward daily replacement value from a shared default-off adapter. post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: The fast filing-lag source did not clear the canonical Gate 4 bar. The result suggests SEC periodic timeliness by itself is not a distinct standalone candidate pool under next-open execution and accepted source comparators. Its historical value may be as a support feature inside fundamental-growth selection rather than as a separate event-led entry source.

prediction.confidence_reason: SEC periodic-report absorption and SEC financing item-code scouts failed, but filing timeliness is a different free PIT field. The positive precedent is exp-20260601-027 Companyfacts filing timeliness support; this run asks whether the same timing edge can stand alone as a production-visible SEC event candidate source.

production_impact.parity_note: This experiment changes no production code. A positive result remains only a replay lead. Promotion would require one shared default-off adapter that loads the same PIT SEC filing event rows, computes the same report-date-to-filing-date lag thresholds, applies the same signal-date OHLCV leadership envelope, overlap exclusion, next-open paper entry, 10-trading-day exit, costs, cooldown, comparator, and concentration guards in historical replay and daily production before any report queue, paper ledger, candidate priority, sizing, watchlist, or order surface could change.
